_status: Sam explained what three confusingly-similar fields in the new student report actually mean, which is what made them safe to load. Two of them describe things nothing we hold has ever recorded: how far an articulation has got through approval, and which steps of the CPL process a college has ticked off. Both reports are now loaded into a holding area and compared against the live tables, college by college. Everything lines up, and the two colleges that looked like they had LOST records turned out to have had those records simply moved to a newer catalog year. Nothing live has been changed yet: switching the new data in would raise the headline "units waiting to be acted on" figure by about 7%, and that is Sam's call to make knowingly rather than find out afterwards.

items.text: The refreshed MAP data is loaded and checked, but not switched on yet. Turning it on raises the headline figure — units of credit sitting unacted-on — from about 1.05 million to about 1.13 million, and the number of students from 42,346 to 47,804. Nothing is wrong with either number; the new one is simply more current. Worth a nod from you before it changes on the dashboard, since that million-unit figure is the one we lead with everywhere.

The new report records "transcribed" in two different places, and they disagree by more than three times: 82,235 rows where a college has ticked the transcribing step as done, but only 25,621 where an actual number of units was recorded. Every row with units also has the tick, so neither is wrong — they answer different questions. Which one should the dashboard mean when it says "transcribed"? (Same call you made before about "applied", where you said publish both and name the gap.)

Worth knowing before anyone designs around it: the approval-stage field you described is empty on 91% of rows, and where it is filled the commonest value is "Implementation" rather than "Initiator". So it can tell us about a slice of the data, but it cannot be used to break the whole backlog down by stage — a chart built on it would describe under 9% of rows while looking like it described all of them.

Once Sam has nodded: switch the refreshed data in following docs/map_custom_report_load.md, rebuild the two published summary tables in the same pass so the public and internal figures never disagree, and restore the two tables' access rules SEPARATELY — they are not the same, and getting them the wrong way round would quietly expose student-level rows to everyone with a team passphrase.

Should this refresh run automatically? It is deliberately manual right now — an automatic nightly rebuild of a table holding 500,000+ student-level rows felt like something to be chosen rather than assumed. Happy either way once you have seen a refresh land.

Ashley is meeting San Joaquin Delta College with a list of 42 occupations where the college already teaches the content and the MAP credit recommendation already exists. Worth knowing how it lands — and if Delta corrects any of our matches, those corrections are the most useful thing to come back with, because they tell us where our course-matching was wrong.

Delta teaches a utility/hydroelectric apprenticeship — turbines, protective relaying, high-voltage switching, aqueduct systems — covering 6 jobs with NO credit recommendation anywhere in California. The question to ask the college is who sponsors that apprenticeship, because that sponsor is who any new MAP exhibit would be built around. This would be first in the state.

Delta runs a full 10-course plumbing apprenticeship, but it is filed under no plumbing-named program, so it does not show up in a program search and MAP does not know Delta has it — the statewide plumbing contractor exhibit lists Delta on neither side. Worth asking the college directly whether other pathways are hidden the same way.

Delta has no fire technology instruction at all, and fire is the biggest block on the SJCOE list (17 occupations) and the best-covered in the state. So those students either get referred elsewhere — Modesto has the largest career portfolio in California — or Delta decides to build a fire program. That is a decision for the meeting, not something we can fix.

Three decisions still open on splitting the public site from the internal one, all from Session 169 and none of them urgent: does the public Knowledge Base stay CC BY 4.0 (it currently lets anyone reuse the methodology commercially — the highest-leverage of the three); are we on GitHub Free or Team (Free cannot publish a site from a private repo, so it decides what is possible); and does the CPL-Initiative GitHub organisation have a second owner yet? Pedro was added on Supabase but GitHub was never confirmed.

Still outstanding after three sessions: run a SECOND partner's occupation list through the statewide crosswalk engine and work whatever it cannot match. Until that happens, the claim that coverage builds up across partners is a design intention rather than something we have shown.

After Ashley's Delta meeting, record which of the 42 the college accepted, rejected or corrected into kb/delta_offering_map.json. The corrections are the highest-value input — they are the only signal that tells us where our judgment about a course was wrong.
